concerns.text: FR-016 states that response‑time measurements will be obtained from an auxiliary crowdsourced experiment and merged with Moral Machine records using `scenario ID` and `participant pseudonym`. The public Moral Machine dataset does not contain any participant‑level identifiers that can be linked to a separate experiment, making such a merge infeasible. Consequently, the primary outcome variable (log‑RT) cannot be aligned with the temperature predictor, breaking the independence between predictor and outcome and rendering the core hypothesis (temperature → response speed) unsolvable with the described data.

FR-003 requires fitting a mixed‑effects model with log‑transformed response time as the dependent variable, yet the outcome variable is unavailable for the Moral Machine records (see FR-016 issue). Modeling on a fabricated or mismatched response‑time column would be circular and invalid.

FR-004 lists covariates (age, gender, etc.) that are to be included alongside the missing response‑time outcome. Because the outcome cannot be measured for the same participants, any inference about the temperature effect is scientifically unsound.

SC-002 defines statistical significance of the temperature coefficient (p < 0.05) as a success criterion, but without a valid, matched response‑time outcome the p‑value is meaningless; the validation target (significant coefficient) is not independent of the predictor construction.
